newsitem.title: USA: Digital cuts prices on workstations, servers.
newsitem.headline: Digital cuts prices on workstations, servers.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp said it cut its prices on servers and workstations which run on its 64-bit Alpha microprocessors by as much as 40 percent or more.
The cuts reflect the increased competitive positioning for Digital's workstation products, volume manufacturing and lower-priced memory for its AlphaServer line, Digital said.
The price cuts on Digital's AlphaStation workstations are effective in Europe and the U.S. and cuts on its AlphaServer systems are effective worldwide.

Among the cuts, the price of Digital's midrange AlphaServer 4000 5/300 system with 512 megabytes of RAM will drop 47 percent to $31,500. Digital's AlphaServer 8200 5/440 with two gigabytes of memory falls 20 percent to $224,400.

Digital's AlphaStation 600/333 with 128 MB of memory was cut 42 percent to $24,995 and its AlphaStation 500/500, which it calls the world's fastest desktop workstation, with 128 MB of memory drops 20 percent to $39,995.
Digital also said it introduced new base-level server configurations that provide as much as four times the memory of current systems at little or no extra cost.

"Reducing AlphaStation prices is a key element of Digital's continued drive to provide desktop visual computing excellence to our customers," Philippe Ribeyre, vice president of Digital's workstation business segment, said in a statement.
